method: Inspect every distinct SVG on Chromium contact sheets; reopen dense or ambiguous examples at native size. Reuse a review only when SVG SHA-256 bytes match. Scores are subjective visual judgments, separate from semantic and geometry assertions. After discovery, every one of the 220 distinct sources was recompiled in each of five complete confirmation passes; every SVG byte hash matched its inspected image.

rubric.beauty: 5: no observed material spacing, alignment, shape, clipping or connector defect at readable/native zoom; 4 or below: a concrete visual improvement remains.
rubric.clarity: 5: the stated concept, directions, ownership, captions and attachments are unambiguous at readable/native zoom; 4 or below: a concrete communication problem remains.

limitations: Bounded authored concepts and seeded grammars, not all possible input graphs.
Dense graphs can require panning; a full-fit thumbnail is not the legibility standard for a large diagram.
Crossing minima are asserted for named graph families only; arbitrary graphs have no global optimality proof.
One Chromium/Linux font environment; authored hard constraints and diagnostic controls are evaluated separately.
